explanation: Fires on the word that opens a predicate's complement right after a subject plus copula, auxiliary, modal or predicate adjective: strongest (over half of max) on focus 'only' after a modal or copula (can only, will only, it's only), on a preposition or 'to' completing a readiness, ability or approval predicate or a light verb (ready to/for, able to, good at, looks great on, runs well on, got/kept on, its way into, Come/Hold on), and moderately on a preposition straight after a copula (it is on/in/at/under) or on adverbs after a modal (will also, has always), plus any '@'. It stays below a quarter of max on the same prepositions after an action verb or its object (sat/jumped on, put it in, crashed into, spoke with, dug in), in fixed verb collocations (based on, click on, listened to, relied on), after trying, sorry, angry, tired, interested or bad, inside noun phrases (picture of, letter from), on sentence-initial 'Only' and 'Not only', and on nouns and determiners in plain noun phrases.
